1.explanation: In the React version of the Search component (Search.js), the render() method injects the magnifier icon (<Search16>) with role="img" but fails to provide any accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby). That omission triggers the DAP violation. To fix it, render() must either mark the icon as aria-hidden (if purely decorative) or supply a meaningful aria-label (for example, set aria-label={labelText} on the <Search16> element). Adjusting render() in Search.js resolves the violation.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the DOM for the Carbon Search component in Safari with VoiceOver enabled and DAP running. The magnifier icon is rendered as an <svg> (via the Search16 React icon) with role="img" but no aria-label or aria-labelledby. DAP flags this as a WAI-ARIA violation because any element with role="img" must supply non-empty accessible text, otherwise screen readers cannot announce it.

2.explanation: The Search class’s render() method renders the <Search16> icon with role="img" but fails to supply an accessible name. Any element with role="img" must include either an aria-label or aria-labelledby to provide non-empty alternate text. To fix the violation, the render() method should add an aria-label (for example using the labelText prop) to the Search16 icon.
2.bug_scenario: When running the Carbon React Search component under VoiceOver (macOS) with DAP enabled, the search magnifier icon is rendered with role="img" but no aria-label or aria-labelledby. This causes the DAP violation “The WAI-ARIA widget with IMG role must have a nonempty alternate text or a label.”
